_readme: Topics and concepts for CSW2.
Concepts carrying prerequisite_course CSW1 are what the diagnostic tests: a
sem-4 student is expected to arrive with them. The rest are current-course
material and exist so practice and misconceptions have somewhere to hang.
EVERY concept here was checked against the ingested corpus with the FULL
evidence check -- retrieval similarity AND the entailment call -- before being
added. Similarity alone is not enough to choose a syllabus, and we found that
out the hard way:
'Python classes and objects' scored 0.7206 similarity, comfortably above the
0.70 gate, and then failed entailment at 0.15. The Django book uses classes on
every page and never once teaches them, so there was nothing to build a
remedial lesson out of. Its gap lesson correctly refused -- which is the right
behaviour and the wrong content decision.
Same reason, same measurement: 'HTML forms and input fields' scored 0.49 (the
book covers Django form RENDERING, not HTML form basics) and 'Model fields and
field types' 0.56.
Two of those three are still listed below, WITHOUT a prerequisite_course, and
that distinction is the whole fix. Only a prerequisite concept is testable by
the diagnostic, and only a diagnostic wrong answer creates a gap whose lesson
has to be generated -- so a concept with no prerequisite_course is never asked
to teach itself out of a corpus that cannot. They stay listed because the
seeded practice items and the misconceptions behind seven confirmed heatmap
diagnoses hang off them; deleting them silently empties two heatmap rows.
'Model fields and field types' is genuinely absent -- nothing references it.
CONTENT LEAD: before adding a concept, run the evidence check against the
corpus. A concept the book cannot teach produces insufficient_evidence on its
gap lesson, which breaks golden path step 2 without breaking any test.
